terms.meaning: Informal name for the visible front assembly. It can include dial, hands, markers, apertures and displays.
The surface carrying markings and/or openings beneath the hands; not every display has a conventional dial.
The way time or information is shown: hands, discs, numerals, satellites, rolling elements, LCD and other arrangements.
Band is the umbrella term. Strap usually means flexible material. Bracelet usually means linked or mesh construction.
The structural material of the case. Specify alloy/grade, purity or composite formulation separately.
The surface appearance or treatment: polished, brushed, blasted, engraved and related choices.
A layer applied over a substrate. PVD is a deposition process. DLC is a carbon coating family and can be deposited using different processes.
Appearance does not establish material: gold-tone can be a coating or color on an inexpensive substrate.
Stones used on dial, bezel, case, crown or bracelet. Natural, laboratory-grown and simulant choices differ.
Usually synthetic ruby bearings and related components inside the movement; separate from exterior decoration.
Any capability such as reading time, timing a lap, sounding an alarm, navigation or displaying a sensor measurement.
An added mechanical function beyond basic timekeeping, such as calendar, chronograph or repeater.
A software data widget on a watch face; the term differs from the mechanical use.
A regulating architecture intended to address positional effects; not itself a calendar, timer or additional displayed function.
A stopwatch function that can start, stop and usually reset elapsed-time measurement.
A timekeeper meeting a defined accuracy/testing criterion. Certification scheme and test conditions must be specified.
Mechanical watch wound by wrist motion through a winding mechanism. Some related electronic architectures also harvest wrist motion.
Seiko/Grand Seiko architecture using a mainspring for power with quartz-reference electronic regulation.
Light-emitting material on components. Modern photoluminescent pigment requires charging by light.
Sealed gaseous light sources powered by radioactive decay. They need no prior charging and become dimmer with age.
Timex brand for electrically powered dial/display illumination; distinct from passive photoluminescent paint.
Qualitative design-family classification, not a promise of current stock, compatibility, cost or custom manufacturability.
Diameter, width, thickness, length, curvature, shades and artwork are parameters, so no finite option list exhausts every value.
Dial apertures, hands, calendar position, stem position, pushers and display layouts must match the chosen movement or a purpose-designed system.
Movement diameter/thickness, crystal geometry, caseback, gaskets and crown/pushers constrain the case assembly.
Matching lug width alone is insufficient. Bar diameter/position, case curvature, lug clearance and clasp attachment also matter.
The rating applies to the assembled tested watch. Material or a screw-down crown alone does not establish the rating.
Radium paint and older tritium paint are historical categories. They are not ordinary new-build material choices.
Available measurements and alerts depend on hardware, software, model, region and any required authorization. No universal diagnostic accuracy is implied.
Choose the movement and display first, then case dimensions, material/finish, crystal, controls, illumination and strap/bracelet. Validate fit and functions together.
